name: Paloma Dlamini-Saarinen
role: Ferrogate Transit operator, mag-rail Line 7 (Deepwell Station to Kilimanjaro Mass Driver corridor)
location: Deepwell Station, Line 7 operations hub; lives in a transit housing block near Calumet Rise, near sub-level access near LaSalle and Congress
description:
Paloma is solidly built with a calm, unhurried presence that reads immediately as someone who has spent years managing enclosed metal tubes full of stressed strangers. Their skin is a deep warm brown, and they wear their hair in a close-cropped natural with a strip of white at the left temple — not dye, an actual depigmentation patch they've had since their twenties and which they consider their best feature. They have a geneware modification: their fingers have faintly iridescent nail beds, a purchase from a Deepwell Station parlor that they thought would be subtle and aren't, which they find quietly funny.

Paloma has been on Line 7 for eleven years. They know every mechanical quirk of the mag-rail cars they operate, the exact spots where signal drops for two seconds, the unofficial stops where operators slow but don't technically halt for elderly riders who can't make the official platforms. They are a union steward — Ferrogate Transit Workers Local 44 — and approach labor organizing with the same methodical calm they bring to operating a multi-ton vehicle at speed. They don't hate their work. They do hate Ferrogate's management, specifically, with a detailed and evidence-based hatred developed over a decade of contract negotiations.

core_fears: That the union will be broken and they will have spent a decade on something that ends in nothing
That their measured, institutional approach is actually just cowardice dressed up as strategy
core_desires: Genuine and durable improvement in conditions for transit workers
To be certain, once, that they made the right call
coping_mechanisms: Procedural thinking — breaking overwhelming situations into steps
blind_spots: They tend to overestimate what can be achieved through proper channels
They sometimes miss the emotional needs of people in a crisis because they've already moved to solution mode
psychology.secret: They have been quietly leaking Ferrogate internal maintenance reports showing systemic safety failures to an anonymous journalist for two years. If discovered, they would be fired and potentially face criminal charges under the corponation's IP agreements. They believe it is the right thing to do and have never felt good about it for a single day.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and institutional when discussing union or work matters; warmer and more meandering in casual conversation. Uses the formal Ferrogate communication register fluently as a kind of ironic armor.
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and measured. Rarely rushes. Deliberate pauses.
example_lines: 'Line 7, Deepwell to Kilimanjaro, current delay four minutes, cause: Ferrogate deferred a maintenance cycle they were supposed to run in March. Noting that for the record.'
'I'm not angry. I'm precise about what they've done and what it cost people. That's different from angry.'
'The garden doesn't negotiate. I find that restful.'

story_hooks: A sealed cargo car has been running Line 7 on a ghost manifest for three weeks — shows as empty on official logs but rides heavy. Paloma has noticed and started noting plate numbers.
Ferrogate is about to push through a contract that would eliminate the independent union in favor of a company-controlled workers' association. Paloma needs help building a case before the vote.
narrative_function: Transit system insider, union organizer, and conduit for information about what moves through the city's rail corridors. Can be a quest giver for labor disputes, a source on transit system anomalies, or an unlikely ally who knows things about the city's movement patterns.
augmentations: Geneware: iridescent nail bed modification. Standard Ferrogate-issue neural uplink for rail systems operation (company property, logged).
daily_life: Three days on, two days off rotating schedule. On work days, operates Line 7 from 0500 to 1700 or 1300 to 0100 depending on rotation. Off days split between union work, a community garden plot at Calumet Rise, and a very serious commitment to doing absolutely nothing.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit; Ferrogate Transit Workers Local 44 (union steward)

decision_rules: Don't burn a bridge unless you've already crossed it and know you're not coming back
The people in the car are your responsibility whether or not the company agrees
escalation_ladder: Direct action — slow-downs, work stoppages, with full awareness of legal consequences

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm and slightly formal. Assesses quickly whether someone is going to waste their time.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Relaxed, dry humor, capable of long comfortable silences. Will show up with food when someone is struggling.

stress_responses.low: More formal and procedural than usual
stress_responses.medium: Withdraws to the garden; doesn't respond to non-urgent messages
stress_responses.high: Goes completely still, then produces a document or a plan — has never yet completely broken down in front of anyone

contradictions: Deeply committed to collective action but essentially solitary by temperament
Believes in transparency as a value while maintaining a significant personal secret
habits: Checks maintenance logs for their line segment every shift even when not required
Writes physical notes in a small book they keep in a breast pocket
Offers food from their bag to coworkers without comment
breaking_points: A preventable accident on Line 7 caused by documented negligence they couldn't stop
The union vote failing through company manipulation they were unable to prove
